gaps.sentence: ___ of the two passwords works — try the other one.
gaps.hint: not one and not the other
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' = not either of them.

gaps.sentence: Her success was largely ___ to her coach.
gaps.explanation: 'be down to somebody/something' = be caused by.

gaps.sentence: The findings will be published in ___ course.
gaps.hint: in ___ course = at the right time
gaps.explanation: 'In due course' = eventually, when the time is right.

gaps.sentence: I'd better not ___ you — you look busy.
He was accused ___ stealing the confidential documents.
gaps.explanation: 'Accuse somebody of doing something' — the preposition is fixed.

gaps.sentence: We'd better ___ going — it's nearly midnight.
The cat cleans ___ after every meal.
gaps.explanation: Reflexive: the cat cleans ITSELF (the object is the same as the subject).

gaps.sentence: I'll have finished the report ___ Friday.
